events.evidence_text: The voice gives useful directions and calls you 'friend'. It knows you have no pulse before you tell it.
events.dialogue: Stay near the lanterns. You always hated the dark.
events.speaker: Unknown Voice
events.next_mystery: Who is speaking, and how does it know what you fear?

events.evidence_text: Your name is listed as a gunshot victim. The close-range wound and a familiar shell casing do not match the voice's claim that the gangsters killed you.
events.dialogue: The handwriting is yours. The date is the night your friend said you would meet.
events.speaker: Thought
events.next_mystery: Why did your friend arrange to meet you on the night you died?

events.evidence_text: A torn page speaks of satisfaction and a lifeline, but its central clause is missing. The margins warn: 'Do not trust a copy made by the interested.'
events.dialogue: Two names are crossed out. The sentence explaining why has been cut away.
events.speaker: Thought
events.next_mystery: Who removed the most important line from the contract?

events.evidence_text: A delivery for the night of your death lists blood bags, a clean shirt, and a route out of the settlement. The recipient is marked 'F'.
events.dialogue: That shipment was for your friend. He came here looking for a way to get you out alive.
events.speaker: The Butcher
events.next_mystery: Did your friend try to save you before he pulled the trigger?

events.dialogue: I opened the back door. Your friend told me to keep it open. Then I heard the shot.
events.speaker: The Butcher
events.next_mystery: If the Butcher left a way out, why did your friend stay?

events.evidence_text: A carbon copy shows a clause overwritten in fresh ink. It says the lifeline requires 'at least one' fallen enemy; a later hand added 'exactly'.
events.dialogue: I corrected a dangerous ambiguity. That is what you wanted to hear, isn't it?
events.speaker: The Strategist
events.next_mystery: Who wrote the original contract, before the Strategist changed its meaning?

events.evidence_text: The trap route guides you toward a chamber marked as a witness stand. Its mechanism records who chooses violence when a safe path is available.
events.dialogue: The traps were never meant to stop you. I wanted to see what you would choose.
events.speaker: The Strategist
events.next_mystery: Who is the unseen witness judging your choices?

events.evidence_text: The stone bears the unaltered wording: 'A lifeline is granted when at least one named enemy is fully satisfied.' Nothing says exactly one. By defeating both, you qualify.
events.dialogue: AT LEAST ONE. Not exactly one. The contract did not forbid your revenge; someone forged that restriction.
events.speaker: The Pact
events.next_mystery: Why does the lifeline return you to the living while keeping your soul tethered here?

events.evidence_text: The rift repeats the same breath hitch heard in your friend's last voicemail. The voice is not the friend speaking live; it is an echo bound to his pact mark.
events.dialogue: I was there. I tried to stop it. The rest of the memory is missing.
events.speaker: Unknown Voice
events.next_mystery: Why did your friend bind his own voice to the pact?

events.evidence_text: From the doorway, your friend raises the gun. From the reflected window, the Strategist stands behind him holding the contract's bloody seal. Both images are true; neither includes the order the friend refused.
events.dialogue: I did pull the trigger. I won't ask you to call that mercy.
events.speaker: Your Friend
events.next_mystery: What was the Strategist forcing your friend to choose between?

events.evidence_text: Your friend learned the Strategist planned to use your living soul as a permanent anchor. He tried the Butcher's escape route first. When the ritual began, he shot you to break the binding before the Witness could claim you. He hid his voice in the pact so you could learn the truth, knowing you might never forgive the murder.
events.dialogue: I chose your death over letting it own you forever. I was wrong to choose for you. I am still responsible.
events.speaker: Your Friend
events.next_mystery: Who—or what—is the Witness that wrote a contract no dead soul remembers signing?

events.dialogue: I cannot undo the shot. I will spend what remains trying to keep the Witness from choosing for anyone else.
events.speaker: Your Friend
events.next_mystery: The Witness's true name remains hidden beyond the last gate.

events.dialogue: You refuse his forgiveness. The tether breaks, but the Witness is still out there, listening.
events.speaker: Your Friend
events.next_mystery: The Witness's true name remains hidden beyond the last gate.
